# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 61 (Bi-Vb Pc61)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc61

**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 61
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 61. Ordaining a pregnant woman
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining a pregnant woman

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 61 (titled *Gabbhinī*) prohibits a Buddhist nun from ordaining a pregnant woman, designating such an act as an offence of expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Horner, Cullavagga]. According to the casuistry, an exception (*anāpatti*) applies if the ordaining nun does not know or genuinely believes that the candidate is not pregnant [Horner, Cullavagga]. In the commentary *Samantapāsādikā*, the term for a pregnant woman (*āpannasattā*) is glossed as one into whose belly a living being has entered (*kucchipaviṭṭhasattā*) [Hüsken 1997]. Within the sequence of ordination rules (Pācittiyas 61–83), the causative verb *vuṭṭhāpeti* specifically denotes conferring full ordination (*upasampadā*) within the community of nuns [Hüsken 1997]. Modern scholars note that Pācittiya 61—together with Pācittiya 62 concerning nursing mothers—depicts women receiving ordination directly without the mandatory two-year probationary training (*sikkhamānā*), an institutional requirement that later rendered such rules practically redundant, since pregnancy would become manifest over a two-year probation [Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels for this rule exist in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pc 61) and Parivāra (Pc 61), as well as in the nun-rules of the Dharmaguptaka (Dg Bi Vb Pc 119), Mahīśāsaka (Mi Bi Vb Pc 116), and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan (xct-mu-bi-vb-pc87) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus demonstrates substantial text reuse within the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, showing close verbatim formulaic parallels with Pācittiya 62 (§0.1–2.2.3 ↔ §0.1–2.16), Pācittiya 82, and Pācittiya 74, along with cross-language textual alignments in Tibetan Vinaya treatises and Jayarakṣita's Sanskrit commentary *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
